paragraphs.title: A Cry from Fear and Distress

easy.explanation: He asks God to hear his prayer and supplication.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist ask to give ear to his prayer?

easy.explanation: He says that the terrors of death have fallen upon him.
easy.q: What has fallen upon the psalmist?

easy.explanation: He wishes for wings like a dove so that he could fly away and be at rest.
easy.q: What does the psalmist wish he had wings like?

answers: Because of the enemy, oppression, fear, and distress
Because he wants to see a new land
Because he is tired of worshiping
medium.explanation: The enemy, the wicked, and fearful circumstances cause him to seek escape.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist desire to flee?

answers: I would quickly seek a place of safety
medium.explanation: He wants to escape quickly from the storm and tempest.
medium.q: What does “I would hasten my escape” mean in context?

answers: From prayer and fear to a desire to flee
medium.explanation: He first asks God to hear him, then describes fear and longs to escape.
medium.q: How does the psalmist’s response develop in these verses?

answers: He wants to defeat his enemies by force
He longs to get away from danger and find rest
He wants to summon people to battle
challenge.explanation: The dove expresses his longing to fly away from distress and find a quiet refuge.
challenge.q: What does the image of the dove reveal about the psalmist’s desire?

challenge.explanation: His fear and trembling correspond to the windy storm and tempest.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the psalmist’s inward condition and the storm?

answers: He does not want to speak about his trouble
He sees bringing his cry before God as the first step toward help
He thinks God is hiding in the city
challenge.explanation: His appeal for God’s attention shows that he brings his distress before God.
challenge.q: What does his request that God hear him suggest?

paragraphs.title: A City Filled with Violence and Deceit

easy.explanation: He says that he saw violence and strife in the city.
easy.q: What did the psalmist see in the city?

easy.explanation: The city is surrounded by trouble continually, both day and night.
easy.q: When do trouble and wickedness surround the city?

easy.explanation: Deceit and guile do not depart from the city’s streets.
easy.q: What is found in the streets?

medium.explanation: The verses describe violence, sorrow, wickedness, deceit, and guile.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the condition of the city?

medium.explanation: Here, “mischief” refers to trouble and harm within the city.
medium.q: What does “mischief” mean in this context?

answers: Because they speak words of peace
Because he wants them to learn another language
Because the city is filled with violence, strife, and deceit
medium.explanation: The request follows his description of violence, quarrels, and deception.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the Lord to divide their tongues?

answers: The corruption and danger continue without stopping
The city is empty at night
challenge.explanation: The words “day and night” stress the continual nature of the evil.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the violence being present day and night?

answers: The walls protect the city from every evil
The walls themselves are made of deceit
The danger surrounds the city and is also within it
challenge.explanation: The trouble goes about the walls while wickedness and deceit remain inside.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the walls and the condition of the city?

answers: The city suffers from both wrongdoing and deception
The only problem is a lack of food
The people refuse to speak to one another
challenge.explanation: The terms present both dishonest conduct and misleading speech.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the pairing of “deceit” and “guile”?

paragraphs.title: The Betrayal of a Close Companion

answers: A close companion, guide, and acquaintance
easy.explanation: The psalmist identifies the betrayer as a man who had been his equal, guide, and acquaintance.
easy.q: Who was the person that caused the psalmist’s deepest pain?

answers: Taken sweet counsel and walked to the house of God
easy.explanation: They had shared counsel and gone together to the house of God.
easy.q: What had the psalmist and this companion done together?

answers: The two men had never met
easy.explanation: The injury comes from someone who had once been close and trusted.
easy.q: What makes the betrayal especially painful?

answers: The close companion had shared trust, counsel, and worship with him
The enemy lived in another city
medium.explanation: The companion’s former closeness and shared worship made the betrayal more grievous.
medium.q: Why could the psalmist have endured an enemy’s reproach more easily?

answers: We shared intimate counsel and conversation
medium.explanation: The phrase describes close and meaningful fellowship.
medium.q: What does “we took sweet counsel together” mean?

medium.explanation: A trusted companion became a source of painful opposition.
medium.q: What change in the relationship is described?

answers: They were looking for a hiding place
They were enemies in the city
challenge.explanation: Their fellowship included going together to worship God.
challenge.q: What does the mention of walking to the house of God emphasize?

answers: It shows that the companion was unimportant
It shows a sharp change from deep trust to betrayal
It proves the psalmist did not know him
challenge.explanation: The former equality and friendship make the later betrayal especially shocking.
challenge.q: Why does the contrast between an equal and an enemy intensify the passage?

answers: He distinguishes expected attacks from the unexpected wound of a close companion
He wants everyone to become his enemy
challenge.explanation: His pain is heightened because the reproach came from someone trusted, not from a normal enemy.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement, “it was not an enemy that reproached me”?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Justice and Security in Prayer

easy.explanation: He says that he will call upon God and that the Lord shall save him.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist call for salvation?

easy.explanation: He names evening, morning, and noon as times of prayer.
easy.q: At what times does the psalmist pray?

easy.explanation: He trusts that God will hear his voice.
easy.q: What does he believe will happen to his prayer?

answers: A desire merely to announce the time
That he has forgotten his trouble
medium.explanation: Prayer at evening, morning, and noon shows continual reliance on God.
medium.q: What does praying at three times of day show about the psalmist?

answers: Speaking and crying out in anguish
medium.explanation: The words describe bringing his sorrow before God with a loud cry.
medium.q: What does “I mourn in my complaint, and make a noise” express?

answers: Judgment for the wicked and salvation for himself
Peace for the wicked and punishment for himself
Escape into the wilderness for everyone
medium.explanation: He asks God to deal with the wicked while trusting God to deliver him.
medium.q: What does the psalmist seek for the wicked and for himself?

answers: He combines a desire for justice with active trust in God
challenge.explanation: He seeks justice against evil while continuing to pray and depend on God.
challenge.q: What does the movement from judgment to prayer reveal about the psalmist?

answers: He has been rescued from conflict and brought into peace
He has gone out to begin a war
challenge.explanation: The psalmist describes God delivering him safely from the battle against him.
challenge.q: What does “He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle” mean?

answers: They limit prayer to one moment
They portray prayer continuing throughout the day
They show that he prays only during emergencies
challenge.explanation: The repeated times create a picture of continual prayer and dependence.
challenge.q: How do “evening, and morning, and at noon” strengthen the message?

answers: As people who do not fear God
easy.explanation: The passage says that they fear not God.
Although his words are smooth, war is in his heart.
easy.q: What lies behind the enemy’s smooth words?

easy.explanation: The command is to cast the burden upon the LORD.
easy.q: Upon whom is the righteous person told to cast his burden?

answers: The enemies trust God while the righteous deceive
The enemies hide war behind smooth words, while the righteous rely on the LORD
The enemies pray while the righteous flee
medium.explanation: The enemies are treacherous, but the righteous are told to place their burden upon God.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between the enemies and the righteous?

answers: Give your trouble and care to the LORD
Throw an object into the city
medium.explanation: The command means to entrust one’s burden and care to God.
medium.q: What does “Cast thy burden upon the LORD” mean?

answers: The LORD will not suffer him to be moved
He will never meet an enemy
medium.explanation: The LORD promises to sustain the righteous and not let him be moved.
medium.q: What is promised to the righteous?

answers: Outward words may hide inward hostility
The enemies speak with complete honesty
challenge.explanation: The contrast shows that pleasant speech does not reveal the enemy’s true intentions.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between “smoother than butter” and “war was in his heart”?

answers: It expresses hope that God will protect the righteous and judge the wicked
It cancels the request for judgment
It proves that the wicked have already been saved
challenge.explanation: God’s support of the righteous stands against the destruction awaiting the wicked.
challenge.q: How does the promise concerning the righteous relate to judgment on the wicked?

answers: The psalmist adopts the ways of the wicked
He ends by expressing confidence in God despite danger
challenge.explanation: After describing violence and deceit, he closes with a declaration of trust in God.
challenge.q: What does “but I will trust in thee” accomplish at the end of the psalm?
